 Honda, Ford, BMW and Harley-Davidson Vehicles Recalled
 Free Press Publisher 
 November 16, 2026 
 Lifestyle and Travel News , Notices 
 A National Highway Traffic Safety Administration recall notice lists eight recalls involving Honda, Acura, Ford, BMW and Harley-Davidson vehicles for steering, braking, electrical and other issues.
 Honda and Acura 
 Recall 26V721 concerns a potential loss of power steering assist in 2022–2024 Acura MDX, 2021–2025 Acura TLX and 2023–2025 Honda Pilot vehicles.
 A separate recall, 26V735 , covers 2024 Acura ZDX vehicles for an unexpected loss of brake pressure.
 Ford 
 Three Ford recalls are included:
 26V724: A loose 12-volt cable may cause a loss of drive power in 2022 Maverick Hybrid vehicles.
 26V725: Windshield wipers may detach on 2026 Bronco vehicles.
 26V726: Map lights may remain illuminated in 2026–2027 Explorer vehicles. The notice identifies Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 101.
 Harley-Davidson 
 Recall 26V730 concerns a neutral-gear display that may indicate neutral when the transmission is actually in gear.
 Affected 2026 models include FLHX, FLHXL, FLHXLSE, FLHXSE, FLHXSTSE, FLTRX, FLTRXL, FLTRXP and FLTRXSTSE.
 BMW 
 Recall 26V731 concerns incorrect high-voltage battery charging software in 2026–2027 i5 eDrive40, i5 M60 xDrive and i5 xDrive40 vehicles, along with 2027 i7 xDrive50 and i7 xDrive60 vehicles.
 Recall 26V733 carries a park-outside warning because a water pump connector may short circuit. Affected models are:
 Model Model years 
 228i, 228xi 2014–2016 
 328i, 328xi 2012–2016 
 428i, 428xi 2014–2016 
 528i, 528xi 2012–2016 
 X1 2012–2015 
 X3 2013–2017 
 X4 2015–2018 
 X5 2016–2018 
 Z4 2012–2016 
 Owners can enter their license plate or vehicle identification number in NHTSA’s recall lookup tool to check whether their specific vehicle has an unrepaired recall. Owners with an open recall should contact their dealership to arrange a free repair.

 The Franklin County Free Press, established by Vicky Taylor in 2019, emerged as a beacon of local journalism for the residents of Franklin County. Under Vicky's leadership, it quickly became an essential source of news, particularly at a time when major newspaper publications were increasingly overlooking local coverage. 
On January 1, 2022, the torch was passed to Nathan Neil and his firm, Neil Publishing, LLC. Neil, a local entrepreneur with multiple thriving businesses in Chambersburg, shares Vicky's fervent commitment to both the community and the world of local journalism. 
Rooted in the heart of Franklin County and powered by its residents, the Franklin County Free Press continues to bridge the gap, ensuring that the local stories, events, and issues that matter most to the community remain in the spotlight.
